bullets.title: July CPI soft, core PCE tracking ~21-23bp — September hike odds fall to ~36%
bullets.body: July core CPI printed +0.22% m/m in line with consensus; supercore eased to +2.84% y/y. Morgan Stanley forecasts core PCE at +0.23% m/m (revised up from +0.20% on portfolio management fee noise that BEA will strip out post-September). Wolfe flags the bar for a September hike is higher post weak July employment, with Street consensus core PCE in low 20bp range — insufficient to move the FOMC. September cut odds fell from ~47% pre-release to ~36%.

bullets.title: PPI mixed but friendly: headline flat, goods -0.7%, core services +0.59%
bullets.body: July headline PPI came in flat (-0.03% m/m) vs. +0.2% consensus; core PPI +0.2% vs. +0.3% expected. PPI energy fell -3.1%; core goods softest since late 2024. International airfares -12.1% m/m offset a 6.5% jump in portfolio management fees. Initial claims 209k (vs. 202k expected) but 4-week average flat at 199k; labor market described as broadly healthy.

bullets.title: CreditSights sees Fed on hold through H1 2027; JPM raises S&P PT to 8,000
bullets.body: CreditSights forecasts the Fed holds rates through all of 2026 and H1 2027 as inflation settles at 3.4% and wage/payroll trends soften. JPMorgan separately raised its 2026 S&P 500 PT to 8,000 (2026 EPS $365, +35% y/y), while flagging structurally higher volatility, a December 2026 FOMC hike, and 10-year yields at 4.85% year-end. Yield curve long steepener position hit cycle highs on the CPI print.

bullets.title: Inflation picture nuanced: 41% of core CPI categories >4% annualized, drug prices at record low
bullets.body: Despite the benign headline, 41% of core CPI categories are running above 4% annualized m/m — a broadening of underlying price pressure. Prescription drug prices fell -0.8% m/m (-3.1% y/y), fastest decline on record. Rent/OER settling into 2.5-3% range. 22V notes Hormuz disruption and AI-related durable goods pricing as upside inflation tail risks.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro: flows/passive positioning driving tape; USD weakness engineered; Warsh Fed hawkish
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags 2026 tape is driven by passive and levered flows, not Mag 7 fundamentals. High-beta momentum was +69% YTD on June 22 then went negative YTD five weeks later despite S&P +12.5% YTD. USD intervention was coordinated between Treasury and Japan in July via FIMA facility expansion. Warsh Fed maintains hawkish bias with a hike still on the table.

bullets.title: Tape setup constructive: small caps at ATH, 8/11 sectors up, S&P gamma supportive below 7,750
bullets.body: Small caps trading at all-time highs; 8 of 11 sector styles rose yesterday. Russell 1679 companies reported +31% y/y EPS acceleration. Oppenheimer notes gamma is supportive below SPX 7,750 with dealers long calls; negative gamma above 7,800. Leveraged ETF AUM down 42% from June to $154B with re-leveraging expected as vol falls. 93% of S&P companies are in open buyback window.

bullets.title: Jefferies: AI capex bottlenecks building; TMT ex-Mag 7 now at 97th percentile crowding
bullets.body: Jefferies flags ~25% of major planned data center builds (40% of planned capacity) face delays from component shortages, permitting, labor, and power. Hyperscaler cloud backlogs reached $2.3T. HF TMT ex-Mag 7 exposure at 97th percentile vs. 54th percentile for Mag 7, a notable crowding shift. S&P rally driven by fresh longs, not short covering — short base at 91st percentile creates vulnerability.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex >$1.5T in commitments; funding demand competes with government financing needs
bullets.body: Hyperscalers have made purchase commitments exceeding $1.5 trillion. AI-related investment-grade issuance now ~25% of net Treasury issuance absorbed by private investors (up from 5% in 2025). One analyst flags this creates material market funding pressure alongside large government deficit financing. JPM's Nowak estimates ~20-60% ROIC on 1GW of owned compute even at lower token pricing.

bullets.title: BofA raises 2030 server CPU market forecast to $210B+ on AI agent demand
bullets.body: BofA revised its 2030 server CPU market forecast to $210B+ (from $170B), nearly 5x the estimated 2025 market size, as AI agents shift CPUs from supporting roles to orchestration/control-plane functions. The call implies a potential structural shift in CPU-to-GPU ratios within AI infrastructure builds.

bullets.title: Tech conf day 1 takeaways: TTD headwinds broader than guided; ADBE margins under pressure; TEAM upbeat
bullets.body: Citi TMT channel checks from tech conference: TEAM management upbeat on seat expansion, cloud migration, and AI momentum via Teamwork Graph/MCP; DKNG prediction market timing matters (NFL Sept launch neutral, NBA late-Oct launch negative near-term); TTD facing headwinds broader than discussed on earnings call; ADBE margins pressured by freemium transition costs ahead of usage scaling; PINS sounding better on engagement.

bullets.title: MS TMT: LITE outperforms on margins; CSCO -6% on GM miss; COHR -7% disappoints
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes LITE beat Q2 with 50.4% GMs (+140bps vs consensus), MSR raised PT to $1,000. CSCO fell ~6% on lower gross margin guidance despite strong AI orders — hardware mix headwinds offsetting Enterprise/Hyperscale demand. COHR fell ~7% on low-end GM expectations despite revenue beat. Pattern emerging from Citi: Q2 'Buy the Group' shifting to Q3 'Buy the Stock' with clear pair trades (ANET vs CSCO, LITE vs COHR/GLW, STX vs WDC).

bullets.title: CRWV and NBIS beat; neocloud fundamentals strong with >$25B early-Q3 commitments
bullets.body: CoreWeave beat on active power and margins with >$25B in early-Q3 commitments; Blackwell pricing at new highs with CoreWeave raising prices ~25%. Nebius beat topline and raised FY26 contracted power targets. Both names fell ~1.5-2.5% in pre-market on positioning, not fundamentals. Compute demand described as tight with high-beta momentum in neocloud names.

bullets.title: Mizuho: DELL up 288% YTD, bullish on COHR reaching 42%+ GMs; NVDA near June highs into Aug 26 earnings
bullets.body: Mizuho's Klein flags DELL has 50-60% revenue growth and 85-100% EPS growth; COHR guiding to $3B quarterly revs within 4 quarters (vs consensus $2.7B) and will achieve then exceed 42% GM target with CPO ramp on track for 2H27. NVDA at ~$224 near June highs with Aug 26 earnings as next key test; new $500B financing fund reduces circularity concern by bringing in pension/insurance/SWF capital.

bullets.title: Oil falls 2%+: higher US crude inventories, IEA/OPEC demand cuts, Iran Hormuz spill nearing end
bullets.body: Brent and WTI crude futures fell more than 2% (WTI at $81.20 pre-market) on higher US crude inventories and reduced demand projections from both IEA and OPEC. Iran's Strait of Hormuz oil spill cleanup reached its final stages. Jefferies noted Hormuz tensions are showing up in refining crack spreads and risk premia rather than outright crude price spikes.

bullets.title: Tariff enforcement strained; Navarro flags USMCA transshipment provision, customs overwhelmed
bullets.body: US Trade Adviser Navarro confirmed USMCA renegotiation will include strict transshipment provisions to prevent third-country circumvention. Navarro separately said US customs officials are overwhelmed by tariff evasion attempts. JPM research notes tariff regime likely to feature differentiated rates: ~3-4% Canada/Mexico, ~15% allies, ~18-20% ASEAN/South Asia, higher for China.

bullets.title: DOL pushing 401(k) access to private markets — structural tailwind for large alt managers
bullets.body: DOL Acting Secretary is pushing expansion of 401(k) access to alternative investments including private credit, infrastructure, real estate, and PE. JPM views retail 401(k) as the largest untapped capital pool; permanent/semi-permanent capital would be fee-rich and less cyclical. Largest scaled alt platforms with wealth distribution capabilities (BX, APO, KKR, BAM) are best positioned.

bullets.title: Misery Index fell to 7.5% in July; MBA mortgage apps rebound +3.6%, 30-yr rate dips to 6.77%
bullets.body: The Misery Index (CPI + unemployment rate) rolled over in July to 7.5%, supported by moderating inflation and a slight unemployment downtick. MBA mortgage applications rebounded +3.6% for the week ended Aug 7 after a -2.9% prior decline; 30-year rate fell to 6.77% from 6.81%, its first decline in six weeks. Manhattan median rents hit a record $5,000 in July (+6.4% y/y) with listing inventory down 39%.

bullets.title: AMD files debt shelf; S&P 500 futures +0.22%, 10Y yield -4bp to 4.65%
bullets.body: AMD filed an automatic debt shelf registration (S-3ASR) of indeterminate amount, with the 424B5 follow-on also filed at a stock price of $482.93. Broader pre-market context: S&P 500 futures +17 points (+0.22%) to 7,787.5; 10-year yield down 4bp to 4.65%; WTI -2.49% to $81.20. DELL +4% and HPE +3.4% on Lenovo sympathy; CRM +1.9% after JPMorgan resumed Overweight.

bullets.title: DeepSeek introduces peak/off-peak API pricing effective Aug 16; competitive AI pricing pressure continues
bullets.body: DeepSeek announced a new tiered API pricing structure (peak and off-peak rates) taking effect August 16. The move adds competitive pricing pressure on frontier model providers and hyperscaler inference offerings, consistent with the broader trend of open-weight models gaining share per Morgan Stanley's Ramp July data (open-source gaining share; Anthropic leads business penetration at 43.5%, OpenAI at 39.7%).

bullets.title: Qatar LNG force majeure: 56 cargoes unshipped, September supply unclear; European gas supply pressured
bullets.body: Qatar has not shipped 56 LNG cargoes since invoking force majeure, with no clarity on whether September supply will resume. European gas supply faces additional pressure, partially offset by increased US LNG cargo availability. Separately, European heatwaves are reducing French nuclear output by 15% on Friday, with Romania shutting its sole working reactor due to low Danube levels.
